sk.teks: This is grammar focused lesson so listening, speaking, reading and writing skills are not explicity covered

sp.teks: This is grammar focused lesson so listening, speaking, reading and writing skills are not explicity covered

sk.teks: By the end of Form Six / Matriculation / IPGM Preparatory Programme, students can: Identify main points and ideas

sp.teks: Understand the information content of the majority of recorded or broadcast audio materials on topics of personal interest
Understand recordings in the standard form of the language and identify speaker viewpoints and attitudes as well as the information content
Understand a wide range of recorded and broadcast audio material, and identify finer points of detail including implicit attitudes

sk.teks: Listen for specific details and important information

sp.teks: Recognise the speaker’s point of view and distinguish this from fact and opinion
Understand the speaker’s point of view on topics that are of current issues
Follow complex lines of argument in a clearly articulated lecture
Follow lectures, talks and reports and other forms of academic or professional presentations
Follow most lectures, discussions and debates with relative ease
Understand announcements and messages on concrete and abstract topics
Understand complex technical information, such as operating instructions, specifications for familiar products and services
Follow chronological sequence in extended informal speech such as in a story or an anecdote
Identify the main reasons for and against an argument or idea in a discussion conducted in clear standard speech
Easily follow complex interactions in group discussion and debate on abstract, complex and unfamiliar topics

sk.teks: By the end of Form Six / Matriculation / IPGM Preparatory Programme, students can: Exchange personal or factual information

sp.teks: Give clear, detailed descriptions on a wide range of subjects related to one’s field of interest
Give a clear, detailed description of how to carry out a procedure
Give a clear, systematically developed presentation, with highlighting of significant points, and relevant supporting detail
Deliver announcements on most general topics with a degree of clarity, fluency and spontaneity
Communicate detailed information reliably
Describe the personal significance of events and experiences in detail
Take a series of follow up questions with a degree of fluency and spontaneity which poses no strain for either oneself or the audience
Understand in detail what is said to one in the standard spoken language
Convey degrees of emotion and highlight the personal significance of events and experiences
Use telecommunications for a variety of personal and professional purposes, provided one can ask for clarification
Develop a clear argument, expanding and supporting one's points of view at some length with subsidiary points and relevant examples
Give a clear, prepared presentation, giving reasons in support of or against a particular point of view and giving the advantages and disadvantages of various options
Explain a viewpoint on a topical issue giving the advantages and disadvantages of various options
Summarise and give his or her opinion about a short story, article, talk, discussion interview, or documentary and answer further questions of detail
Outline an issue or a problem clearly, speculating about causes or consequences, and weighing advantages and disadvantages of different approaches
Express one's ideas and opinions with precision, present and respond to complex lines of argument questions
Engage in extended conversation on most general topics in a clear and participatory fashion
Participate actively in formal and informal discussion in familiar contexts, commenting and putting point of view clearly
Sustain one's opinions in discussion by providing relevant explanations, arguments and comments
Carry out an effective, fluent interview, departing spontaneously from prepared questions, following up and probing interesting replies
Easily follow and contribute to complex interactions in group discussion in complex unfamiliar topics
Make critical remarks or express disagreement diplomatically

sk.teks: By the end of Form Six / Matriculation / IPGM Preparatory Programme, students can: Understand main points and ideas

sp.teks: Identify the main conclusions in clearly signalled argumentative texts
Read and understand specialised articles outside one's field
Read and identify the content and relevance of news items, articles and reports on a wide range of professional topics
Read and obtain information, ideas and opinions from highly specialised sources within one's field

sk.teks: Locate specific details and important information

sp.teks: Read correspondence relating to one's interest and understand essential meaning
Read a personal email or posting even where some colloquial language is used
Read and scan through long and complex texts from several sources (news items, articles, reports, websites, books etc.) locating relevant details
Read and understand articles and reports concerned with contemporary problems in which the writers adopt particular stances or viewpoints
Recognise different structures in discursive text: contrasting arguments, problem solution presentation and cause-effect relationships
Read and understand implicit as well as explicit attitudes, emotions and opinions in a text
Read and understand instructions and procedures in the form of a continuous text, for example in a manual
Read and understand lengthy, complex instructions in one's field, including details on conditions and warnings
Make basic inferences or predictions about text content from headings, titles or headlines
Deduce the probable meaning of unknown words in a written text
Identify unfamiliar words from the context on topics related to one's field and interests
Extrapolate the meaning of a section of a text by taking into account the text as a whole
Exploit different types of connectors and the role of key paragraphs in the overall organisation, in order to better understand the argumentation in a text
Use a variety of strategies to achieve comprehension, including reading for main points; checking comprehension by using contextual clues
Read newspaper or magazine accounts of films, books, concerts etc. and understand the main points
Read for pleasure, adapting style and speed of reading to different texts (e.g. magazines, novels, biographies, travelogues, guides, lyrics, poems)
Read novels or short stories that have a strong, narrative plot and that are written in straightforward language
Read contemporary literary texts and non-fiction written in the standard form of the language with appreciation of implicit meanings and ideas

sk.teks: By the end of Form Six / Matriculation / IPGM Preparatory Programme, students can: Organise content and ideas

sp.teks: Write an essay or report that develops an argument systematically with appropriate highlighting of significant points and relevant supporting detail
Write a detailed description of a complex process
Evaluate different ideas or solutions to a problem
Synthesise information and arguments from a number of sources
Write a suitable introduction and conclusion to a longer report or article on a complex academic or professional topic provided that the topics is one's field of interest
Write a review of a film, book or play
Write clear detailed descriptions of real or imaginary events and experiences on a variety of subjects
Write a detailed critical review of cultural events or literary works
Post online accounts of social events, experiences and activities and sharing personal feelings
Write letters conveying degrees of emotion and highlighting the personal significance of events and experiences and commenting on the correspondent’s news and views
Write non-routine professional letters using appropriate structure and conventions
Use idiomatic expressions and colloquialisms in correspondence and other written communications
Write formal correspondence such as letters of enquiry, request, application and complaint with appropriate register, structure and conventions
Take or leave complex personal or professional messages
State and respond to opinions on topics of interest in an online discussion
Write informal correspondence using the language fluently and effectively to give detailed descriptions of experiences, pose sympathetic questions and follow up issues of mutual interest
Write personal and professional letters and emails using appropriate formality and conventions
Write formal correspondence such as letters of clarification, application, recommendation, reference, complaint, sympathy and condolence with good expression and accuracy
